gist: Native communities in the US south-west are recovering from severe El Niño-driven floods.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Unprecedented rain intensified by El Niño caused once-in-a-generation flooding in the Four Corners region. The San Juan River crested at 21ft near Shiprock, causing wastewater treatment facilities to fail and sewage to enter the river. Residents were ordered to evacuate, and homes, farms and roads were submerged.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The floods created severe biohazards with high levels of E coli and treatment chemicals in soil and water. Farmers lost entire crops and face heavy financial losses, while tribal trust land issues complicate crop insurance. Displaced families struggle with power outages and lack clear support.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Evacuees in temporary housing must secure funds for deposits to extend their stay. Communities and local groups continue providing food, supplies and animal shelter while residents await safe road conditions to begin rebuilding.
